newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman signs $50 million oil deal with Saudi firm.
newsitem.headline: Oman signs $50 million oil deal with Saudi firm.

text.p: Oman on Saturday signed a $50.5 million oil exploration deal with Nimir Petroleum Company Ltd. of Saudi Arabia.

The concession covers an area of 15,000 square km in bloc three in northeast Oman, Petroleum and Minerals Minister Saed bin Ahmed al-Shanfari told reporters after signing the agreement with the company's chief Abdullah Mohammad Bansudan.
"They can start working as of tomorrow (Sunday)," Shanfari said.

The Saudi company will conduct geophysical and geological studies in the first phase of the project before agreeing with the oil ministry on a location to drill two deep wells to look for oil and gas, Bansudan said.
No further details on the agreement were available.
Oman produces 900,000 barrels per day of oil -- which accounts for nearly three-quarters of government revenue.
